# Volume 1 — CHAPTER XIX. A Concert, a Catastrophe, and a Confession

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

“THIRZA, may I pop across to visit Isolde for a brief moment?” inquired Nell, as she hurried out of breath down from the east gable during an evening in February.
{: #nw-v01-c19-p0000 }

“I cannot understand your need to be wandering around once it is night,” Thirza stated abruptly. “You and Isolde made the journey from school to home alongside one another and subsequently remained down there in the snow for an additional thirty minutes, your tongues moving without pause, clickety-clack. Therefore, I do not believe you are in a dire situation regarding another meeting with her.”
{: #nw-v01-c19-p0001 }

“However, she desires to meet with me,” begged Nell. “There is something of great importance she must say to me.”
{: #nw-v01-c19-p0002 }

“In what way are you certain of her doing so?”
{: #nw-v01-c19-p0003 }

“Since she only now sent me a sign from her window. A method of signaling using our candles and cardboard has been organized by us. Putting the candle upon the window sill, we create flashes as we move the cardboard to and fro. A specific number of flashes signifies a particular message. The notion belonged to me, Thirza.”
{: #nw-v01-c19-p0004 }

“I’ll guarantee you that it was,” Thirza stated with emphasis. “And before long you will be igniting the drapes with your ridiculous signaling.”
{: #nw-v01-c19-p0005 }

“Oh, we exercise great caution, Thirza. And it is quite fascinating. A pair of flashes signifies, ‘Are you there?’ A trio signifies ‘yes’ and a quartet ‘no.’ A quintet signifies, ‘Come over as soon as possible, because I have something important to reveal.’ Isolde transmitted five flashes just now, and my curiosity to discover what it is causes me real agony.”
{: #nw-v01-c19-p0006 }

“Indeed, there is no need for your continued distress,” Thirza remarked with sarcasm. “Your departure is permitted, yet your return must occur within precisely ten minutes, keep that in mind.”
{: #nw-v01-c19-p0007 }

Nell indeed recalled it and returned prior to the deadline, even if perhaps no living human will truly grasp what she endured to keep the conversation regarding Isolde’s significant news from exceeding ten minutes. Yet she had certainly employed that time effectively.
{: #nw-v01-c19-p0008 }

“Oh, Thirza, guess what? You are aware that Isolde’s birthday is tomorrow. Well, her mother gave her permission to invite me to come to her house after school and sleep over with her. And her cousins are traveling from Stonebridge in a large pung sleigh so they can attend the Debating Club concert at the hall tomorrow evening. And Isolde and I will be taken to the concert by them—provided you give me permission to go, of course. You will allow me, won't you, Thirza? Oh, I am so thrilled.”
{: #nw-v01-c19-p0009 }

“You can relax now, since you are staying behind. It is preferable for you to be at home resting in your bed, while that club concert is sheer foolishness, and young girls ought never to be permitted to attend those sorts of venues.”
{: #nw-v01-c19-p0010 }

“I feel certain that the Debating Club represents a thoroughly commendable organization,” Nell offered in defense.
{: #nw-v01-c19-p0011 }

“I am not denying that it is. However, you will not start wandering off to musical performances and remaining out until all hours. What fine behavior for youngsters. I find it surprising that Mrs. Pembroke is allowing Isolde to attend.”
{: #nw-v01-c19-p0012 }

“However, it is a truly remarkable event,” lamented Nell, almost weeping. “Isolde celebrates just a single birthday each year. Birthdays are hardly frequent occurrences, Thirza. Sukey Pullen intends to declaim ‘Curfew Must Not Ring Tonight.’ Thirza, that work possesses such an excellent moral, and listening to it would certainly benefit me immensely. Furthermore, four beautiful, touching pieces—which are almost as fine as hymns—will be performed by the choir. And oh, Thirza, the minister will participate; yes, truly, he will deliver a speech. It will be practically identical to a sermon. May I please go, Thirza?”
{: #nw-v01-c19-p0013 }

“Nell, you heard my words, didn't you? Go to bed now after taking off your boots. It is after eight.”
{: #nw-v01-c19-p0014 }

“There’s merely a single additional detail, Thirza,” Nell remarked, possessing the demeanor of someone delivering their final remaining argument. “Mrs. Pembroke informed Isolde that the spare-room bed was available for us to sleep in. Consider the prestige of your own little Nell being placed in the spare-room bed.”
{: #nw-v01-c19-p0015 }

“That is a distinction you must manage to do without. Retire for the night, Nell, and ensure I do not hear a single additional word from you.”
{: #nw-v01-c19-p0016 }

As soon as Nell had proceeded mournfully to the upper floor, her cheeks wet with weeping, Obed, who seemed to have been fast asleep on the couch throughout the entire conversation, unclosed his eyes and uttered with conviction:
{: #nw-v01-c19-p0017 }

“Well now, Thirza, it seems to me you should allow Nell to go.”
{: #nw-v01-c19-p0018 }

“I do not, in that case,” Thirza snapped back. “Obed, which one of us is raising this child, you or me?”
{: #nw-v01-c19-p0019 }

“Well now, you,” conceded Obed.
{: #nw-v01-c19-p0020 }

“In that case, do not meddle.”
{: #nw-v01-c19-p0021 }

“Listen here, I’m not stepping in. Holding a personal view doesn’t mean stepping in. And I hold the view that you should allow Nell to leave.”
{: #nw-v01-c19-p0022 }

“I do not doubt you believe I should allow Nell to travel to the moon were she inclined,” Thirza pleasantly replied. “Had that been the sole matter, I perhaps would have permitted her to pass the night alongside Isolde. However, I am against this idea of a concert. She would likely contract a cold in that place, while her mind became burdened with foolishness and agitation. For seven days, she would remain disturbed. Obed, my grasp of that child's temperament and its proper care exceeds yours.”
{: #nw-v01-c19-p0023 }

“I feel you should allow Nell to go,” Obed insisted once more. Reasoning was hardly his fort, yet clinging tenaciously to his view undoubtedly was. Thirza let out a helpless gasp and retreated into quietness. On the following morning, while Nell was cleaning the breakfast dishes inside the pantry, Obed stopped prior to leaving for the barn so he could repeat to Thirza:
{: #nw-v01-c19-p0024 }

“It is my opinion that you should permit Nell to leave, Thirza.”
{: #nw-v01-c19-p0025 }

For an instant Thirza's expression conveyed thoughts forbidden to be spoken. Thereafter she submitted to the unavoidable and remarked sharply:
{: #nw-v01-c19-p0026 }

“All right, she is allowed to leave, because you will not be satisfied with anything less.”
{: #nw-v01-c19-p0027 }

With a sodden dishcloth clutched in her hand, Nell rushed abruptly from the pantry.
{: #nw-v01-c19-p0028 }

“Oh, Thirza, Thirza, utter those holy words once more.”
{: #nw-v01-c19-p0029 }

“I suppose speaking them a single time suffices. This is the work of Obed, and I disclaim all responsibility for it. Should you contract pneumonia from slumbering in an unfamiliar bed or emerging from that stifling hall during the dead of night, do not hold me accountable, hold Obed accountable. Nell Harcourt, greasy water is leaking from you all across the floor. A child so heedless I have never witnessed.”
{: #nw-v01-c19-p0030 }

“Ah, I am well aware of what a heavy burden I am to you, Thirza,” Nell uttered with remorse. “My blunders are so numerous. Nevertheless, consider the vast number of errors I refrain from making, despite being capable of them. Prior to leaving for school, I will fetch sand to scour these marks away. Oh, Thirza, attending that performance was the absolute desire of my soul. Never have I attended a concert in all my days, and whenever my classmates discuss them at school, I feel entirely excluded. The depth of my emotions regarding this was unknown to you, whereas Obed perceived it clearly. Obed comprehends my nature, and being comprehended brings such joy, Thirza.”
{: #nw-v01-c19-p0031 }

Nell was far too thrilled that morning in school to perform properly in her lessons. In spelling class, Hugh Carrow bested her, and he completely outdistanced her when it came to mental arithmetic. Nevertheless, because of the concert and the bed in the spare room, Nell suffered less embarrassment than she otherwise would have. Throughout the entire day, she and Isolde conversed about these matters so incessantly that had their teacher been anyone less lenient than Mr. Pidgeon, severe punishment would undoubtedly have been their fate.
{: #nw-v01-c19-p0032 }

Nell believed she would have found it unbearable had she not been planning to attend the concert, since no other topic was talked about in school that day. Several minor free entertainments had been hosted by the Brierley Debating Club, which convened every two weeks throughout the winter; however, to raise funds for the library, this event was going to be a grand occasion with an entrance fee of ten cents. For weeks, the Brierley youth had been rehearsing, and because their elder siblings were participating, all the pupils felt a particular interest in it. Apart from Carrie Mott, whose father held the same views as Thirza regarding young girls attending evening concerts, every student in school above nine years old anticipated attending. Throughout the afternoon, Carrie Mott wept over her grammar book and considered life to be devoid of value.
{: #nw-v01-c19-p0033 }

The genuine thrill started for Nell when school was dismissed, building in a steady crescendo from that moment on to a climax of sheer bliss during the performance itself. A “perfectly elegant tea” was enjoyed by them; after which followed the delightful task of putting on their clothes in the small upper bedroom belonging to Isolde. Isolde styled the front of Nell’s hair using the recent pompadour technique, while Nell used her particular talent to tie Isolde’s bows; additionally, they tried out no fewer than six distinct methods for styling their hair in the back. When they finally finished, their faces were flushed red and their eyes shone with anticipation.
{: #nw-v01-c19-p0034 }

Indeed, Nell was unable to avoid a small ache as she compared her own simple black tam and formless, tight-sleeved coat of homemade gray cloth to the stylish fur cap and fashionable small jacket worn by Isolde. Nevertheless, she recalled just in time that an imagination was hers to employ.
{: #nw-v01-c19-p0035 }

Afterward, the Murrays from Stonebridge, who were Isolde’s cousins, arrived; every one of them packed into the large pung sleigh, nestled in straw and furry robes. Sliding over the satin-smooth roads as the snow crisped beneath the runners, Nell delighted in the ride to the hall. A magnificent sunset occurred, with the snowy hills and deep-blue water of the St. Lawrence Gulf appearing to enclose the brilliance such as a grand bowl of pearl and sapphire filled to the top with wine and fire. From all directions, distant laughter, which sounded like the merriment of wood elves, and the tinkling of sleigh bells resounded.
{: #nw-v01-c19-p0036 }

“Oh, Isolde,” Nell whispered, giving Isolde’s mittened hand a squeeze beneath the fur robe, “doesn't everything seem like a lovely dream? Do I actually appear no different than I always do? My feelings are so changed that I believe my appearance must reveal it.”
{: #nw-v01-c19-p0037 }

“You look remarkably well,” remarked Isolde, who felt compelled to convey the praise to someone else after receiving a compliment from a cousin of hers. “Your skin has the most beautiful flush.”
{: #nw-v01-c19-p0038 }

The performance that evening provided a succession of "thrills" to a minimum of one person present, and Nell promised Isolde that each subsequent excitement surpassed the previous one in intensity. As Sukey Pullen, clad in a fresh waist of pink silk while wearing a pearl necklace around her smooth, pale neck and authentic carnations among her tresses—gossip murmured that these had been ordered from town for her by the schoolmaster—“climbed the slimy ladder, dark without one ray of light,” Nell shuddered with delightful empathy; while the chorus performed “Far Above the Gentle Daisies,” Nell stared toward the ceiling as though angels were painted upon it; as Sam Mott undertook to clarify and demonstrate “How Sockery Set a Hen,” Nell chuckled to the point that neighboring audience members chuckled as well, moved more by rapport with her than by entertainment from a piece that was somewhat worn out even within Brierley; and as Mr. Pidgeon delivered the address of Mark Antony above the lifeless form of Cæsar using extremely deeply moving inflections—gazing toward Sukey Pullen following each phrase—Nell experienced a sense that she could stand up and rebel right then if a single Roman citizen would only take the lead.
{: #nw-v01-c19-p0039 }

A single item on the schedule did not manage to engage her. While Hugh Carrow was performing “Bingen on the Rhine”, Nell took Rhoda Murray’s library book and engrossed herself in it until he reached the end, at which point she remained completely unmoving and rigid while Isolde applauded with enough vigor to make her hands sting.
{: #nw-v01-c19-p0040 }

Their return occurred at eleven, full of indulgence, yet the exceptionally delightful joy of discussing everything remained ahead of them. The residence stood dark and quiet, with everyone appearing to be in bed. Entering the long, narrow parlor—the room from which the spare bedroom led off—Nell and Isolde moved on tiptoe. Dimly illuminated by the glowing coals in the grate, the space felt comfortably warm.
{: #nw-v01-c19-p0041 }

“We should take our clothes off in this spot,” Isolde suggested. “The warmth makes it so pleasant.”
{: #nw-v01-c19-p0042 }

“Hasn’t this been a wonderful experience?” Nell sighed with delight. “Rising to recite in that place must be marvelous. Isolde, do you think we will ever receive an invitation to perform there?”
{: #nw-v01-c19-p0043 }

“Yes, surely, at some point. It is always their wish to hear the great scholars perform. Hugh Carrow frequently does so, even though he exceeds our age by merely two years. Ah, Nell, in what way were you able to act as if you did not hear him? At the moment he arrived at the verse,
{: #nw-v01-c19-p0044 }

‘There is Another, who is not a sister,’
{: #nw-v01-c19-p0045 }

he gazed straight down toward you.”
{: #nw-v01-c19-p0046 }

“Isolde,” Nell stated with composure, “you hold the place of my dearest companion, yet I will not permit even you to discuss that individual with me. Have you prepared for sleep? We should compete in a sprint to determine who reaches the bed ahead of the other.”
{: #nw-v01-c19-p0047 }

The proposal was attractive to Isolde. Down the length of the chamber, past the entrance to the spare room, the pair of small, white-attired forms darted, leaping onto the mattress simultaneously. Subsequently, a movement occurred under their bodies, a breath was drawn sharply alongside a shout, and a voice uttered in deadened tones:
{: #nw-v01-c19-p0048 }

“Merciful goodness!”
{: #nw-v01-c19-p0049 }

Nell and Isolde could not ever explain precisely the way they managed to leave that bed and exit the room. The sole thing they were aware of was that following a single desperate dash, they discovered they were creeping upward on the stairs, shivering as they went.
{: #nw-v01-c19-p0050 }

“Oh, who was it—what was it?” Nell murmured quietly, her teeth clicking together from the chill and terror.
{: #nw-v01-c19-p0051 }

“Aunt Lavinia was the one,” Isolde declared, struggling for breath as she laughed. “Oh, Nell, regardless of how she got to that place, it was Aunt Lavinia. Oh, and her anger is bound to be immense, I am sure. It’s terrible—it truly is terrible—yet Nell, have you ever encountered a thing quite this amusing?”
{: #nw-v01-c19-p0052 }

“Whose name is Aunt Lavinia?”
{: #nw-v01-c19-p0053 }

“She is my father’s aunt, residing in Port Marlow. Her age is tremendous—at least seventy—and I doubt she was ever a small girl. Her visit was expected, yet not this early. Because she is terribly strict and proper, she will give a terrible scolding over this, I am sure. Well, Posy Fay will have to share a bed with us—and you have no idea how much she kicks.”
{: #nw-v01-c19-p0054 }

The following morning, Miss Lavinia Pembroke was absent from the early breakfast. The two little girls received a kind smile from Mrs. Pembroke.
{: #nw-v01-c19-p0055 }

“Was last night enjoyable for you? I attempted to remain conscious until your arrival, because my intention was to inform you that Aunt Lavinia was here and that moving to the upper floor would be necessary for you after all, but fatigue overcame me and I went to sleep. I trust that Aunt Lavinia was not woken up by you, Isolde.”
{: #nw-v01-c19-p0056 }

Isolde kept quietly silent, though she and Nell shared sneaky grins of secret fun from opposite sides of the table. Nell rushed back to her house once breakfast was finished, meaning she stayed happily unaware of the chaos that soon broke out in the Pembroke home until close to evening, at which point she walked over to Mrs. Sowerby’s to do a chore for Thirza.
{: #nw-v01-c19-p0057 }

“So last night, Isolde and you almost scared poor old Miss Pembroke to death?” Mrs. Sowerby asked sternly, though her eye held a twinkle. “A few minutes back, Mrs. Pembroke stopped by here while traveling to Delford. The matter has her feeling genuinely concerned. When old Miss Pembroke rose this morning, she was in a dreadful mood—and I can assure you, Lavinia Pembroke’s temper is nothing to laugh at. She refused to say a single word to Isolde.”
{: #nw-v01-c19-p0058 }

“Isolde was not to blame,” Nell admitted remorsefully. “The responsibility lies with me. My suggestion was that we race each other to be the first one in bed.”
{: #nw-v01-c19-p0059 }

“I was sure of it!” Mrs. Sowerby declared, displaying the satisfaction of someone whose prediction proved right. “I was certain that concept originated from your brain. Well, it has generated a considerable amount of difficulty, that is for sure. Elderly Miss Pembroke arrived to visit for four weeks, yet she asserts she refuses to remain a single day longer and plans to return straight to the city tomorrow, despite it being Sunday. She would have departed today if they had been able to accommodate her. She had undertaken to fund three months of music instruction for Isolde, but at present she is resolved not to assist such a wild girl in any way. Oh, I imagine things were quite chaotic over there earlier today. The Pembroke family must be deeply upset. Elderly Miss Pembroke possesses great wealth, and they would prefer to maintain her favor. To be sure, Mrs. Pembroke refrained from uttering those exact words to me, nevertheless I evaluate people rather accurately, that is for sure.”
{: #nw-v01-c19-p0060 }

“I am a person with such terrible fortune,” Nell lamented. “I am forever tumbling into trouble on my own and dragging my dearest companions—individuals I would willingly die for—into it as well. Are you able to explain to me why this happens, Mrs. Sowerby?”
{: #nw-v01-c19-p0061 }

“That is due to your being overly careless and hasty, young one, that is the reason. You do not ever pause to consider—whatever enters your mind to speak or perform, you speak or perform it without a single instant's thought.”
{: #nw-v01-c19-p0062 }

“Oh, but that is where the finest part lies,” Nell objected. “An idea simply sparks in your head, so thrilling that it forces itself out. Should you pause to reflect upon it, everything is ruined. Have you really never experienced that same feeling, Mrs. Sowerby?”
{: #nw-v01-c19-p0063 }

Indeed, Mrs. Sowerby had done no such thing. Wise-like, she gave a shake of her head.
{: #nw-v01-c19-p0064 }

“You have to acquire the habit of exercising some thought, Nell, that is the issue. The adage you ought to follow is ‘Look before you leap’—above all when jumping into beds in spare rooms.”
{: #nw-v01-c19-p0065 }

A comfortable laugh escaped Mrs. Sowerby regarding her gentle jest, yet Nell stayed thoughtful. No amusement was visible to her in the circumstance, one that seemed extremely grave to her vision. Leaving the residence of Mrs. Sowerby, she directed her steps over the crusty fields toward Pear Hill. At the entrance to the kitchen, Isolde came to meet her.
{: #nw-v01-c19-p0066 }

“Wasn’t your Aunt Lavinia quite upset regarding that?” Nell murmured.
{: #nw-v01-c19-p0067 }

“Yes,” Isolde replied, checking her laughter as she cast a fearful look behind her toward the shut door of the sitting room. “Nell, she was practically leaping in fury. Oh, she gave me such a tongue-lashing. According to her, I am the most ill-mannered girl she has ever encountered, and she declared that my parents should feel disgrace over how they raised me. She claims she will not remain, which certainly makes no difference to me. Father and Mother, however, are concerned.”
{: #nw-v01-c19-p0068 }

“Why didn’t you inform them that I was to blame?” Nell demanded.
{: #nw-v01-c19-p0069 }

“Is it probable that I would act in that way?” Isolde asked with righteous contempt. “Nell Harcourt, I am not a snitch, and besides, the fault was equally mine.”
{: #nw-v01-c19-p0070 }

“Well, I am going inside so that I can inform her personally,” Nell stated with determination.
{: #nw-v01-c19-p0071 }

Isolde stared.
{: #nw-v01-c19-p0072 }

“Nell Harcourt, you wouldn't dare! why—she's going to devour you whole!”
{: #nw-v01-c19-p0073 }

“Do not terrify me beyond the terror I already feel,” Nell begged. “I would prefer stepping in front of a cannon. Nevertheless, Isolde, it is something I must accomplish. The blame rests on me, so I must admit it. Luckily, confessing is something I have practiced.”
{: #nw-v01-c19-p0074 }

“Well, she is inside the room,” Isolde stated. “If you wish to, you may enter. I would not have the courage. Furthermore, I do not think you will accomplish anything at all.”
{: #nw-v01-c19-p0075 }

Buoyed by this reassurance, Nell confronted the beast in its lair—which meant she marched steadfastly to the parlor door and gave a soft tap. A curt “Come in” came next.
{: #nw-v01-c19-p0076 }

Miss Lavinia Pembroke, slender, stern, and unbending, knitted with fury beside the hearth, her anger remaining entirely unsoftened as her eyes flashed behind gold-rimmed spectacles. Turning swiftly in her seat with the expectation of finding Isolde, she met the sight of a pale-faced girl whose large eyes were filled with a combination of wild bravery and fearful hesitation.
{: #nw-v01-c19-p0077 }

“Who are you?” Miss Lavinia Pembroke asked, abruptly.
{: #nw-v01-c19-p0078 }

“Nell of Grey Shutters is who I am,” the tiny guest stated shakily, clutching her hands in her habitual way, “and I have arrived to make a confession, if it suits you.”
{: #nw-v01-c19-p0079 }

“Acknowledge what?”
{: #nw-v01-c19-p0080 }

“That jumping into bed on you yesterday evening was entirely my doing. The idea came from me. I feel certain that Isolde would not have conceived such an action on her own. Isolde behaves in a most ladylike manner, Miss Pembroke. Therefore, you ought to realize that holding her responsible is completely unfair.”
{: #nw-v01-c19-p0081 }

“Oh, is that so, hey? It seems to me Isolde performed at least her fair portion of the leaping. Such behavior occurring within an honorable home!”
{: #nw-v01-c19-p0082 }

“However, our intention was merely to be playful,” Nell continued to argue. “Since we have offered an apology, Miss Pembroke, my feeling is that you should grant us your forgiveness. Furthermore, kindly pardon Isolde and permit her to take her music lessons. Miss Pembroke, Isolde’s desires are deeply tied to her music lessons, and I am all too familiar with the experience of longing for something and being denied it. Should you need to vent your anger on somebody, direct it toward me. Having grown accustomed during my youth to people being angry with me, I am far more capable of bearing it than Isolde is.”
{: #nw-v01-c19-p0083 }

By this point, a glimmer of entertained curiosity had taken the place of most of the fire in the old lady’s eyes. Nevertheless, she continued to speak sternly:
{: #nw-v01-c19-p0084 }

“I do not consider your simply messing around to be an adequate justification. During my youth, young women never engaged in such antics. You fail to understand how it feels when two large girls come leaping directly onto you, rousing you from a deep slumber following an extensive and exhausting voyage.”
{: #nw-v01-c19-p0085 }

“I don’t know, but I can imagine,” Nell said enthusiastically. “It must have been deeply upsetting, I’m certain. However, our perspective exists as well. Do you possess any imagination, Miss Pembroke? Should you have some, merely imagine being in our situation. Having no knowledge that anyone occupied that bed, we were almost frightened to death by you. The feeling we had was completely terrible. Furthermore, following the promise we received, we were unable to sleep in the spare room. Sleeping in spare rooms is something I imagine you are accustomed to. But simply picture how you would feel were you a young orphan girl who had never been granted that kind of privilege.”
{: #nw-v01-c19-p0086 }

By now, every bit of tension had vanished. Miss Pembroke truly uttered a laugh—a noise that made Isolde, who stood waiting in mute apprehension within the adjacent kitchen, draw a deep, relieved breath.
{: #nw-v01-c19-p0087 }

“I am worried my imagination has grown somewhat rusty, as a great deal of time has passed since I last employed it,” she remarked. “I suppose the validity of your request for sympathy matches my own. Everything hinges on our perspective. Take a seat in this spot and describe yourself to me.”
{: #nw-v01-c19-p0088 }

“I am deeply apologetic that I am unable to,” Nell stated with resolve. “It would be my desire, since you appear to be a fascinating woman, and it is possible you are a soulmate even if your appearance does not particularly suggest it. However, returning to the residence of Miss Thirza Abernethy is my obligation. A most benevolent woman, Miss Thirza Abernethy has assumed the responsibility of raising me correctly. She is making every effort, yet the task is exceedingly disheartening. My leaping onto the bed should not cause you to fault her. All the same, prior to my departure, I truly desire that you inform me whether Isolde has your forgiveness and if your visit in Brierley will remain as lengthy as you originally intended.”
{: #nw-v01-c19-p0089 }

“I suppose I might if you drop by to chat with me every now and then,” said Miss Pembroke.
{: #nw-v01-c19-p0090 }

During that same evening, Miss Pembroke presented Isolde with a silver bangle bracelet and informed the household's senior members that her valise had been unpacked.
{: #nw-v01-c19-p0091 }

“My decision is made to remain merely to become more familiar with that Nell-girl,” she admitted openly. “She entertains me, and when one reaches my age, somebody who provides entertainment is uncommon.”
{: #nw-v01-c19-p0092 }

When Thirza listened to the account, her sole remark was, “I told you so.” She directed this toward Obed.
{: #nw-v01-c19-p0093 }

Miss Pembroke remained for the duration of her month and beyond. Because Nell maintained her good mood, she proved to be a more pleasant visitor than she was normally. A strong friendship formed between them.
{: #nw-v01-c19-p0094 }

At the time of Miss Pembroke’s departure, her parting words were:
{: #nw-v01-c19-p0095 }

“Bear in mind, you Nell-girl, that you are to pay me a visit when you arrive in town, where I will lodge you in the most unoccupied spare-room bed I have for sleeping.”
{: #nw-v01-c19-p0096 }

“Miss Pembroke turned out to be a kindred spirit, as well,” Nell admitted to Thirza. “To look at her, you would not believe it, yet it is true. Instead of discovering it immediately, like with Obed, it becomes clear to you only after some time has passed. Kindred spirits are not nearly as rare as I once believed. Discovering that the world holds so many of them is wonderful.”
{: #nw-v01-c19-p0097 }
